issue.title: Update: Multi_Tenant_Security_Cheat_Sheet
issue.body:
## What is missing or needs to be updated?

The Multi-Tenant Security Cheat Sheet is 1,063 lines, and 771 of them are code. The design guidance is good, but the sheet carries full implementations we can't maintain. The biggest blocks are lifecycle (about 154 code lines), logging (143), file storage (107), rate limiting (106) and SQLAlchemy (75).

The sheet also never links the IDOR or Logging cheat sheets, and the Do's and Don'ts list restates every section.

## How should this be resolved?

- Keep each of the 8 sections focused on the design decision and its tradeoffs. The RLS guidance (`SET LOCAL`, `BYPASSRLS`, connection reuse) and the backup-restore guidance are the strongest parts, so keep them.
- Cut the long examples down to the smallest snippet that makes the point, or remove them and link to vendor or framework docs.
- Some requirements live only in code today (for example, revoking sessions and API keys at offboarding). Move those into the prose before cutting the code, and fix any prose that explains a removed example.
- Add links to the [IDOR](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Insecure_Direct_Object_Reference_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html) and [Logging](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Logging_Cheat_Sheet.html) cheat sheets.
- Shorten the Do's and Don'ts so it doesn't restate every section.

Small PRs, one section at a time, please. They are much easier to review than one big rewrite :)

comments.body: I would like to work on this issue, waiting for assignment. thanks

Hi! I'm a third-year AI & Data Science engineering student, and I want to become a regular, long-term contributor to OWASP.

Before choosing a repository, I'd like to understand how new contributors can get started and learn from experienced members of the community.

Could you please guide me on how to begin contributing, and whether there is an official community channel, mailing list, or group where I can connect with project maintainers and get guidance?

I'd like to find a project where I can learn, contribute consistently, and grow with the community over time.

Thank you!

@shiragemalashri-shri Thank you for your interest in contributing. Please begin by carefully studying the [OWASP Cheat Sheet Series](https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/), along with our [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Cheat Sheet Writing Guide](https://github.com/OWASP/CheatSheetSeries/blob/master/GUIDELINE.md). Take the time to read the material, follow its references, and work through the guidance yourself.

That groundwork needs to come first, before asking maintainers for onboarding or proposing contributions. Understanding the existing body of work is necessary both to contribute usefully and to give us enough context to help you.

After that preparation, please bring specific questions: identify the sheet and section you read, explain what you understand, and describe precisely what remains unclear or what improvement you propose. Maintainer time is limited, so we expect you to make that independent effort first.

Please also keep this issue focused on the Multi-Tenant Security Cheat Sheet update. For general community questions after doing that preparation, use the `#cheatsheets` channel on [OWASP Slack](https://owasp.org/slack/invite).

Hi @bhushan4work, thanks again for #2828. Are you planning to continue with the remaining sections (the other long code examples, links to the IDOR and Logging cheat sheets, a shorter Do's and Don'ts)? If we don't hear back by November 10, we'll unassign the issue so someone else can pick up the rest.

@mackowski yes, i'd like to continue working on the remaining sections. thanks for checking!

#2828 covered the tenant onboarding/offboarding section, including moving the session and API-key revocation requirements into prose and removing the lengthy lifecycle implementation.

i'm planning to continue with separate, focused PRs for the remaining sections, starting with logging, followed by file storage, rate limiting, SQLAlchemy, IDOR, tenant identification, and cache isolation. i'll also add the IDOR and Logging cheat sheet references in their respective sections and finish with a shorter Do's and Don'ts list. so this will be a total of 8 more prs so do u want it this way or should I squash them to less no of prs ?? lemme know before I start working on it 

i'll preserve the existing RLS and backup-restore guidance, and make sure any important security requirements currently expressed only in code are retained in the prose before reducing the examples.

Thanks @bhushan4work, the plan looks good! Please keep them as separate, focused PRs, as the issue asks: one section per PR is much easier to review. Two small requests:

- Since all of them touch the same file, please open them one at a time and start the next one after the previous one is merged, to avoid conflicts.
- If a change turns out to be tiny (for example, only adding a cross-link), feel free to fold it into the PR for a neighbouring section. Leaving the Do's and Don'ts for last makes sense, since it depends on what the sections end up saying.

Looking forward to the logging PR!
I ll follow ur instructions. thanks for the heads up.

2907.title: docs: condense malformed XML document and jumbo payload guidance
2907.body:
Refs #2796

- condense guidance for handling malformed xml documents and fatal errors
- clarify that parsers must not continue normal processing after a fatal error, consistent with the [[w3c xml specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-terminology)](https://www.w3.org/TR/xml/#sec-terminology)
- recommend disabling recovery or lenient parsing modes for untrusted input
- streamline coercive parsing guidance and add nesting depth and request size mitigations
- clarify jumbo payload threats as resource exhaustion through memory, cpu, and network bandwidth
- add mitigations for jumbo payloads, including request body limits, parser resource constraints, and streaming parsers
- reference [[oracle jaxp security guide](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/security/java-api-xml-processing-jaxp-security-guide.html)](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/25/security/java-api-xml-processing-jaxp-security-guide.html) for parser limits such as `maxelementdepth` and `entityexpansionlimit`
- remove redundant examples, truncated snippets, and excessive formatting
